knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

```{r library}
library(decisions)
```

## Overview

A rubric lists the ideas that a good answer has. A decision model can check
each idea with a true-or-false question. You can also list the wrong claims
that students often make, and check them in the same way.

This vignette checks short answers to one question about this package:

> What does `decide()` do when one call of a batch fails?

A good answer has four ideas:

* The failed input keeps its row in the output.
* The answers of that row are `NA`.
* The reason of the failure is in the `.error` column.
* The other inputs of the batch still get their answers.

Two wrong claims are common:

* `decide()` stops with an error, or returns nothing, when one call fails.
* `decide()` removes the row of the failed input.

We make one `question_noul()` for each idea and for each wrong claim. All six
questions go into one call of `decide()`, so a student answer costs one call.

The results below come from live calls. The package saved them in
`inst/extdata`, so this vignette builds without a key and without a network.
The code that made them is in `data-raw/vignette_results.R`.

## Rubric

The instructions of each question refer to the text, which is the answer of the
student.

```{r rubric, script = TRUE}
rubric <- list(
  keeps_row = question_noul("Does the text say that the failed input keeps its row in the output?"),
  na_answers = question_noul("Does the text say that the answers of the failed row are NA?"),
  error_text = question_noul("Does the text say that the reason of the failure is in the .error column?"),
  others_continue = question_noul("Does the text say that the other inputs of the batch still get their answers?"),
  stops_all = question_noul("Does the text say that decide() stops with an error, or returns nothing, when one call fails?"),
  drops_row = question_noul("Does the text say that decide() removes the failed input from the output?")
)
```

The student sees only words of the rubric. For each question, we write what
the student sees when the probability is above the threshold of the question
(`if_above`), and when it is below (`if_below`). `NA` means that the student
sees nothing.

```{r rubric-text, script = TRUE}
rubric_text <- tibble::tribble(
  ~question, ~kind, ~if_above, ~if_below,
  "keeps_row", "idea", "Covered: the failed input keeps its row.", "Missing: say what happens to the row of the failed input.",
  "na_answers", "idea", "Covered: the answers of the failed row are NA.", "Missing: say what the answers of the failed row are.",
  "error_text", "idea", "Covered: the reason is in the .error column.", "Missing: say where to find the reason of the failure.",
  "others_continue", "idea", "Covered: the other inputs still get their answers.", "Missing: say what happens to the other inputs.",
  "stops_all", "wrong", "Check again: one failed call does not stop decide().", NA_character_,
  "drops_row", "wrong", "Check again: decide() does not remove the row of a failed call.", NA_character_
)
```

## Sample answers

We wrote 20 sample answers for this vignette. The package has them as the
dataset `rubric_answers`, with the labels. Some answers are good, some have wrong
claims, and some are vague. For each answer, we also wrote a label for each
question: `TRUE` if the answer says it, `FALSE` if not.

```{r samples, script = TRUE}
samples <- rubric_answers
samples[1:3, ]
```

## Setup

`decision_setup()` holds the decider and the six questions. We use Jev. It
reads the key from `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. The saved results below come from the
model `jev-1.14.0`, which the default `"jev-latest"` named on 2026-10-23. In
real grading, give the model a fixed version (for example
`decider_typesafe("jev-1.14.0")`), so that the answers do not change when the
default model changes.

```{r setup-object, script = TRUE}
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe(), rubric)
```

`decide()` takes the setup in place of the decider and the questions. The
answers are the only input.

```{r score, eval = FALSE, script = TRUE}
scored <- decide(setup, text = samples$answer)
```

```{r saved, echo = FALSE}
saved <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "grading.rds", package = "decisions"))
scored <- saved$scored
```

Each question gives its own columns. The column `keeps_row_.pred_true` is the
probability that the answer says it.

```{r probabilities, script = TRUE}
dplyr::select(scored, dplyr::ends_with("_.pred_true"), .error)
```

## Thresholds

A probability is not a grade. For each question, we choose a threshold: the
answer counts as "says it" when the probability is at or above the threshold.
For each question, `yardstick::roc_curve()` gives the sensitivity and the
specificity at each threshold. We take the thresholds that maximize
`sensitivity + specificity - 1`, and then the median of them.

```{r thresholds, script = TRUE}
thresholds <- purrr::map(names(rubric), \(question) {
  tibble::tibble(
    truth = factor(samples[[question]], levels = c(TRUE, FALSE)),
    probability = scored[[paste0(question, "_.pred_true")]]
  ) |>
    yardstick::roc_curve(truth, probability) |>
    dplyr::mutate(j = sensitivity + specificity - 1) |>
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::near(j, max(j)), is.finite(.threshold)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(threshold = median(.threshold), j = max(j))
}) |>
  purrr::set_names(names(rubric)) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "question")

thresholds
```

Twenty answers are few, and we set the thresholds on the same answers that we
use to check them. So the thresholds are rough. Use more labeled answers for a
real course, and keep some of them to check the thresholds.

We join the thresholds to the text of the rubric.

```{r feedback-rubric, script = TRUE}
feedback_rubric <- rubric_text |>
  dplyr::left_join(thresholds[c("question", "threshold")], by = "question")

feedback_rubric
```

## Feedback

`give_feedback()` takes the output of `decide()` for one answer and the
rubric. It returns the lines that the student sees. It never shows a
probability. When the call failed, it says so and shows no provider text.

```{r give-feedback, script = TRUE}
give_feedback <- function(scored, rubric) {
  if (!is.na(scored$.error)) {
    return("The check did not work. Try again.")
  }
  probability <- purrr::map_dbl(rubric$question, \(question) scored[[paste0(question, "_.pred_true")]])
  lines <- ifelse(probability >= rubric$threshold, rubric$if_above, rubric$if_below)
  lines[!is.na(lines)]
}
```

Here are three new answers.

```{r new, eval = FALSE, script = TRUE}
new_answers <- c(
  "The row of the failed call stays in the output. Its answers are NA, and .error has the reason.",
  "decide() stops with an error at the first failed call, and you get nothing back.",
  "It keeps going with the other inputs."
)

new_scored <- decide(setup, text = new_answers)

purrr::map(seq_along(new_answers), \(i) give_feedback(new_scored[i, ], feedback_rubric))
```

```{r show-new, echo = FALSE}
new_scored <- saved$new_scored
new_answers <- saved$new_answers
purrr::map(seq_along(new_answers), \(i) give_feedback(new_scored[i, ], feedback_rubric))
```

## Setup file

`write_setup()` saves the decider and the questions as one JSON file. The file
holds no key.

```{r write-setup, eval = FALSE, script = TRUE}
write_setup(setup, "rubric_setup.json")
```

The thresholds and the text of the rubric are not part of the setup. Save them
as well.

```{r save-rubric, eval = FALSE}
saveRDS(feedback_rubric, "rubric.rds")
```

## Shiny app

The app below lets a student type an answer and press a button. It shows the
rubric text. It uses shiny, which the package does not need. Save
`give_feedback()` in the file `R/feedback.R` of the app folder. Shiny reads
that folder by itself. Put `rubric_setup.json` and `rubric.rds` in the app
folder too. The app needs R 4.3 or newer, because it uses `@` on S7 objects,
and the purrr package, because `give_feedback()` uses it.

`read_setup()` takes a `credentials` function. The function runs when
`decide()` sends the requests. So the host of the app gives the key. On Posit
Connect, for example, you set the variable `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the settings
of the content. The key is a secret of the host. It is never a field of the app
and never in the file.

```{r app, eval = FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(decisions)

rubric <- readRDS("rubric.rds")

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Check your answer"),
  p("What does decide() do when one call of a batch fails?"),
  textAreaInput("answer", "Your answer", width = "100%", rows = 6),
  actionButton("check", "Check"),
  textOutput("provider"),
  uiOutput("feedback")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Replace the function with the key source of your host
  setup <- read_setup("rubric_setup.json", credentials = \() Sys.getenv("TYPESAFE_API_KEY"))

  output$provider <- renderText(
    paste0("Your answer goes to ", setup@decider@provider, " (", setup@decider@base_url, ").")
  )

  output$feedback <- renderUI({
    req(nzchar(input$answer))
    scored <- decide(setup, text = input$answer)
    tags$ul(lapply(give_feedback(scored, rubric), tags$li))
  }) |>
    bindEvent(input$check)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Privacy

The answer of the student goes to the provider that the decider names. With
Jev, that is TypeSafe. The app shows the provider, so the student knows. Read
the terms of the provider before you send student work to it. To keep the
answers on your computer, use a local model. Set the setup to
`decider_systemone()` with a Laya server, as the vignette "Open models on your
own computer" shows. Then the answers never leave the computer.
